property_summary: For any caller, calling transferOwnership either reverts or, if it succeeds, sets owner to the requested new owner; the mutant inverts the check so the owner's own call reverts, leaving owner unchanged and violating the rule.

For any caller, an attempt to call owned() must never alter the stored owner: the owner before the call equals the owner after the call; the mutant breaks this by writing owner = msg.sender inside owned().

For any fuzzed new owner, after ownership is transferred to that address and the new owner calls owned(), the stored owner must remain unchanged (owned() is a state-neutral operation); the mutant breaks this because owned() writes owner = msg.sender, so an owner different from the original deployer ends up replaced by its own address in the observed state sequence.

For any address that currently owns the contract, invoking owned() is a state-neutral operation: it must leave the stored owner exactly as it was (and therefore any later owner may still transfer ownership away to an arbitrary address); the mutant breaks this because owned() writes owner = msg.sender, corrupting the ownership state observed afterwards.

For any fuzzed caller, owned() is state-neutral: it either reverts (non-owner) or, when it succeeds, leaves the stored owner unchanged and preserves the owner's exclusive right to transfer ownership to any address; this general ownership-integrity rule is violated by the mutant only when the caller differs from the stored owner, so the domain is kept wide (caller may be any address including address(0), the deploy-time owner).

For any fuzzed addresses, transferring ownership to a new owner and then having that new owner invoke owned() must leave the stored owner equal to the new owner (ownership stays with the party it was transferred to); the mutant violates this because owned() overwrites the owner with its caller, so any mismatch between the transferred-in owner and a later caller corrupts the recorded ownership.
